subject: Order form: invoice acceptance criteria, tax responsibility & routing
messages:
From: Emily Walker <emily@globex.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Order form questions — invoice routing & tax

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this week. Procurement at Globex asked us to confirm a few commercial details before we sign:

- Who will be responsible for VAT/sales tax remittance (Globex or Redwood)?
- Will Redwood accept split invoicing (first invoice for committed units, then ramp invoices)? If so, what acceptance criteria do you need on our PO?
- We see Net30 on your standard order form; our finance team requires Net45. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept Net45 or if we need to request an exception?

I've attached the order form our legal sent over; we can redline on our side if that helps. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Emily
Emily Walker
Senior Program Manager, Globex Corp

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Emily Walker <emily@globex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:43:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice routing & tax

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Legal (Lauren) and Finance (Marissa) so we can give precise answers and a single redline set.

Quick answers up front:
- Tax remittance: default is Redwood collects and remits where applicable, but we can accept customer withholding if Globex provides a valid tax certificate and we confirm jurisdictional requirements.
- Split invoicing: we support staged invoices. We typically require a PO that references the order form and a clear acceptance checklist for activation invoicing.
- Net terms: our standard is Net30; we can consider Net45 on enterprise deals with a signed amendment.

I've attached our initial redline (Redwood_OrderForm_Redline_v1.pdf) and a blank Tax_Certificate_Template.pdf for your procurement team. Lauren/Marissa — see inline asks below we want to align on before I send back to Globex: 

1) Wording to tie invoice acceptance to "Activation Checklist" vs. "Delivery" — legal preference?
2) If Globex withholds tax, we need a clause requiring timely submission of tax evidence and indemnity for any associated liabilities.
3) Finance: if we agree Net45, any changes to early payment discount or invoice numbering you need?

If it's helpful, I'll propose a simple mutual action plan and target dates.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 1:43 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached our initial redline...

Emily / Globex team — quick legal notes (high-level):

- Invoice acceptance language: recommend we use "Invoice Acceptance Criteria: Activation Checklist completed (appendix A) or written confirmation of activation by Redwood account team." This avoids ambiguous "delivery" language.

- Tax withholding: we cannot agree to blanket customer withholding without a qualified tax residency certificate and a clear indemnity. Proposed clause: customer may withhold taxes only if they provide an accepted tax certificate no later than 30 days after execution; Redwood reserves the right to request supporting documentation and to gross-up where required.

- Net terms: redline keeps Net30 as standard. If Globex requires Net45, add an amendment in the order form that explicitly states "Net45 applies to invoices issued under this Order Form and does not amend other payment obligations under the MSA." This preserves our MSA defaults.

- Attachment: I will upload a short doc with legal margin comments (OF_redline_legal_notes.docx).

Happy to accept minor commercial concessions here but want to avoid open-ended tax exposure.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
(attachment: OF_redline_legal_notes.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Thanks all — finance view below: 

- Invoice routing: we need the PO number on the invoice (exact PO field) and the AP email for remittance (we can accept invoices to billing@globex-ap@). If Globex requires split invoicing, please specify the invoice schedule in the order form appendix (e.g., 40% on activation, 60% quarterly thereafter).

- Acceptance criteria: activation confirmation from our CS team will be sufficient. For forecasting & revenue recognition, we prefer a single activation invoice for committed capacity, then recurring usage invoices. Please note: partial invoices require a corresponding change order or appendix reference.

- Net terms: Net45 is acceptable for this deal, provided: (a) a single amendment confirms Net45 for this order form; (b) Globex agrees to a 1% early-payment discount if paid within 15 days (optional); and (c) we keep standard late fee language (1.5% monthly) to avoid collection risk. If they refuse the amendment path, we need approval from Finance leadership (I can escalate).

Next steps I need from Globex: PO sample, AP contact, confirmation of requested split/invoice schedule.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
